_note: The four open design questions, turned into switchable variables. 'config_key' is a key in the dataset's rules_config. 'decision' is the current choice. Flip a value, run tools/schemacheck.py, and it lists what in the data must change. Source: custom; evidence from ledger pages 00 to 08.

variables.question: One node type with a tree field, or really two trees?

options.two_trees: Science tree and culture tree, each paid with its own yield (reference game).
options.one_tree: One shared tree, a node may be paid with either yield.

variables.rationale: The two trees differ in shape on purpose (wide and branching vs. one steady trunk) and that contrast is the strongest thing in the reference data (ledger 04). The data shape is the same either way, so choosing two_trees costs nothing if you later want one.
metrics: share of nodes finished with a boost
turns spent on each tree per era
number of times the player is blocked by only one yield
variables.how_to_test: Run the same mini-game with each option. In one_tree, watch whether players still need to choose between yields, or whether one yield always wins.

variables.question: Is religion a unit system, or a cultural influence layer?

options.pressure_only: Beliefs spread by pressure from nearby cities and trade routes. No missionary units. Faith is spent on great people and buildings.
options.units_and_pressure: Pressure plus bought spread units with charges (reference game).

variables.rationale: Players complain most about the unit layer: long waves of missionaries across the map, with little defense (ledger 08). The part that works is the belief sentence (condition + filter + yield, ledger 07) and spread by distance. Keep those, drop the units. Faith keeps a job: it buys great people and religious buildings.
metrics: share of cities following a religion by turn
turns until the first religion forms
variables.how_to_test: Run pressure_only and watch whether religion still spreads fast enough to matter by the middle eras. If it stalls, add a pressure multiplier or a small active action before bringing units back.

variables.question: Keep the thin late-game tail of nodes that unlock little?

options.keep: The last tail_eras eras (default 1) may hold thin nodes that unlock nothing and have no boost. Every other node still unlocks at least min_unlocks_per_node.
options.trim: Every node unlocks at least min_unlocks_per_node things, so there is no thin tail.

variables.rationale: Owner decision, overriding the earlier recommendation of trim (8/10). In the reference data the thin tail is only the last era: every node in eras 1 to 7 unlocks something (ledger 07). Keeping it matches the reference and lets the tree end on capstone nodes. The risk is dead-feeling nodes (ledger 08), so two guardrails apply: thin nodes are allowed only in the last tail_eras eras (V3), and a tail node can still carry a direct effect of its own (the example's science tail node does) instead of being a pure prerequisite.
metrics: share of tail nodes the player researches
turns spent on tail nodes as a share of the last era
player reaction to tail nodes (felt pointless or fine)
variables.how_to_test: Play the last era under keep. If tail nodes feel pointless, give each a small direct effect first, and only then try trim. Compare turns spent on the tail under keep and under trim.

variables.question: Is the great-person pool shared between players (needs rivals)?

options.shared_finite: Each person exists once in the world; whoever gets there first claims them (reference game). Works with AI or human rivals.
options.personal: Each community has its own supply of people; no race.

variables.rationale: A civ-style game has rival communities (AI at minimum), so a shared pool gives every player's progress meaning to the others. A personal pool is the safe fallback for a solo mode. The schema supports both with one field.
metrics: share of great people claimed by rivals before the player
points wasted when a person is taken
player complaints about being locked out
variables.how_to_test: Run one game with rivals under shared_finite. If the player is often locked out of a class, add a catch-up discount (as the reference game does for late nodes) before switching to personal.
